html:
The Nhanda are an Aboriginal people of the mid west coast of Western Australia, around the mouth of the Murchison River and present day Kalbarri. They are one of the Yamatji peoples.

Their coast was among the first in Australia touched by Europeans. In 1629 the Dutch ship Batavia was wrecked on the Houtman Abrolhos islands offshore. After a bloody mutiny, two of the mutineers, Wouter Loos and Jan Pelgrom, were put ashore on the mainland, probably in Nhanda country, as punishment. They were never heard of again, and they are often called the first Europeans to live in Australia.

Neighbours on the map are the Malgana around Shark Bay, the Amangu to the south and the Wajarri inland. Sheep stations reached the area in the 1850s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Nhanda are an Aboriginal people of the mid west coast of Western Australia, around the mouth of the Murchison River and present day Kalbarri. They are one of the Yamatji peoples.
